title: Observability Playground & Simulation Lab — Setup Guide
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This page documents the recommended procedure to provision, configure, and operate an Observability Playground: a repeatable, low-cost sandbox that platform operators and SREs use to run controlled degradation, telemetry injection, and tenant-safety simulation experiments. The Playground is intended for operator training, dashboard verification, alert tuning, and pre-rollout validation of runtime changes.

Goals

- Provide a safe, reproducible environment to validate dashboards, alerting rules, and degradation playbooks.
- Enable deterministic injection of degradation signals (latency, error rates, token-cost spikes) tied to synthetic tenants.
- Offer easy cleanup and cost controls so experiments do not affect production billing or shared capacity.

Audience

Platform oncall, SREs, platform operators, operator-training team, and product reliability engineers.

Prerequisites

1. Access: member of the `platform-operators` and `sandbox-admins` groups.
2. Cloud project: a dedicated Playground cloud project with isolated VPC and limited GPU quota.
3. Redis or KV: a local-backed test KV instance (we recommend a small-memory redis-playground cluster).
4. Helm + kubectl: client at platform standard versions (kubectl 1.26, helm 3.9).
5. Workspace: short-lived credentials via vault path `secret/playground/operators`.

Architecture (text diagram)

- Synthetic traffic generator (k8s job) -> Playground ingress (ingress-nginx) -> API route layer (service-mock) -> runtime-mock (prefetcher, kv-cache) -> metrics exporter (statsd/prometheus)
- Telemetry path: metrics -> Prometheus (playground) -> Tempo (traces) -> Loki (logs) -> Grafana (dashboards)

Quick provision checklist

1) Bootstrap cloud project
   - Create project: `rcli projects create --name=observability-playground-<team>-<date>`
   - Apply budget alert: cloud console -> budgets -> threshold 10% of monthly dev budget
2) Create k8s namespace
   - `kubectl create ns observability-playground`
3) Install playground chart
   - `helm repo add rwood-playground https://charts.redwood-inference.net/playground`
   - `helm install playground rwood-playground/playground --namespace observability-playground -f playground-values.yaml`

Recommended playground-values.yaml (example)

apiVersion: v1
kind: Config
metadata:
  name: playground-values
spec:
  ingester:
    replicaCount: 1
  simGenerator:
    cpuRequest: "200m"
    memoryRequest: "256Mi"
    qps: 50
  telemetry:
    prometheus:
      retention: 72h
    loki:
      retention: 72h
  costGuard:
    enabled: true
    monthlyBudgetUsd: 50

(Use the above as a template; keep quotas deliberately small to prevent runaway costs.)

Experiment primitives

- Fault injection: add HTTP latency (ms), 5xx error rate (%), or simulated token surges (tokens/sec) at service-mock.
- Traffic shaping: workloads with different sequence length distributions (short, medium, long) and chat-pattern distributions.
- Prefetch/kv-cache toggles: enable/disable caching to validate fallback and cold-start dashboards.
- Multi-variant routing: route a percentage of requests to a "slow" model variant to test degradation dashboards.

Dashboard and alert onboarding

1. Import dashboard JSON: Grafana -> + -> Import -> `playground-degradation-lab.json` (attached to this page in attachments).
2. Critical panels to verify:
   - Token per request distribution
   - 95th/99th tail latency by tenant
   - KV cache hit-rate by prefix
   - In-flight batches and batch size histogram
3. Alert rules to test:
   - token_cost_spike_playground: trigger when tokens/sec > 3x baseline for > 2m
   - playground_tail_latency_slo: trigger when p99 latency > 1200ms for 5m
4. Verification steps:
   - Start baseline generator: `kubectl apply -f syn-gen-baseline.yaml`
   - Run spike job: `kubectl apply -f syn-gen-token-spike.yaml`
   - Confirm Grafana panels display corresponding signal within 60-90s (Prometheus scrape + Grafana refresh)

Operator runbook (for a standard degradation experiment)

1. Create experiment ticket in the Operator Playground board, fill experiments template (see table below).
2. Provision the lab (Bootstrap checklist).
3. Start baseline traffic and capture baseline metrics (export to /tmp/playground-baseline-<ts>.json).
4. Announce experiment window in #platform-ops (duration and rollback triggers).
5. Run injection with a single toggle (latency OR error OR token spike); do not combine primitives on first run.
6. Observe dashboards for 10 minutes; if alerts fire, follow the Alert Triage Checklist.
7. Tear down injection and run cooldown for 15 minutes.
8. Archive artifacts and retrospective notes to the ticket.

Experiment template (copy into ticket)

- Title: <short description>
- Owner: <operator name>
- Window: <UTC start/end>
- Primitive: latency | error | token_spike | cache_toggle | routing_variant
- Expected impact: <p50/p95/p99 changes, tokens/sec change>
- Safety gates: list of alerts/thresholds that will cause immediate abort
- Cleanup steps: k8s job deletion, costGuard reset, KV flush

Safety & cost controls

Table: Minimum enforced guardrails

| Guardrail                     | Value / Command                                   |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| Monthly budget (USD)         | 50 (playground-values.yaml -> costGuard.monthlyBudgetUsd) |
| Max GPU count                | 0 (CPU-only by default)                            |
| Max QPS per tenant           | 200                                               |
| Alert auto-abort             | If token_cost_spike_playground fires twice in 24h |

Cleanup and post-experiment

- Run `kubectl delete -f syn-gen-*.yaml` to stop generators.
- Remove any persisted KV state: `redis-cli -h $REDIS_HOST FLUSHALL` (playground-only cluster).
- Reset Prometheus retention if exceeded and rotate test indices in Loki.
- Attach artifacts (dashboards snapshot, traces, metrics export) to the experiment ticket.

Practical examples and CLI snippets

- Start single tenant latency inject (example):
  curl -X POST http://service-mock.playground.svc.cluster.local/inject -d '{"type":"latency","ms":350,"tenant":"sim-0"}'

- Run token surge generator (k8s job YAML snippet):
  apiVersion: batch/v1
  kind: Job
  metadata:
    name: token-surge-2024-11
  spec:
    template:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: surge
          image: rwood/playground-sim:latest
          args: ["--mode=token-surge","--qps=450","--tenant=sim-burst"]
        restartPolicy: Never

Oncall verification checklist (fast triage)

1. Confirm whether alerts are Playground-labeled; if so, follow Playground runbook rather than production runbook.
2. Check costGuard dashboard for unexpected spend.
3. If tenant-affecting alert occurs in production, escalate to production runbook immediately.
4. Document time-to-detect and time-to-mitigate in the ticket.

Retrospective & continuous improvement

- After each experiment add a short retro: what telemetry missed the signal, what panels were noisy, what alert thresholds were too sensitive.
- Weekly practice: run one 30-minute desktop exercise in the Playground and record time-to-detect metrics

Roadmap (next 12 months)

- Q1 2025: Add automated experiment runner with parametrized scenarios and reproducible seeds.
- Q2 2025: Integrate small synthetic model variants (quantized) to test end-to-end model swap fallbacks.
- Q3 2025: Cost-aware experiment scheduler that enforces daily budget and operator quotas.

Confidentiality

internal

Last notes

This guide is intentionally pragmatic: keep experiments small, iterate, and record each result. The Observability Playground is a critical training surface to avoid surprises when similar signals appear in production.
